claim: social-media is not 'click the right button'. The checker walks EVERY post and fails on a wrong extra as hard as on a missing one, so the job is to leave the page in exactly one state.

measurement.instrument: full 130 tasks x 5 reps, page identity per rep, exclusive CDP browser
measurement.note: The three repaired tasks went 0/5 -> 5/5 each, verified at 10 reps individually. The paired total reads t=0.82 because ten OTHER tasks drifted down by the same amount -- all of them tasks already known to be unstable at this sample size. The instrument, not the work, is again the limit.

observations: the operand order is not stable: -all/-some put the action first, plain social-media puts the user first
the LABEL is not the CLASS: Mute is li.menu-user, Block is li.block-user, Copy link to Tweet is li.copy
SIX of nine actions live in a ul.hide menu that must be opened first
plain social-media scores ON THE CLICK and compares the class name exactly, so there is no Submit

bug_of_the_round: A hardcoded four-action set ({like,reply,retweet,share}) was still running AFTER the label->class map resolved the action, and overwrote it. 'Mute' resolves to 'menu-user', which contains none of those four words, so every menu action returned social-bad-action while the map was correct. Two correct mechanisms in a row, with a dead one between them.

unstable_task_series.reading: The same code reads 0.00-0.80 on click-collapsible-2-nodelay across five full runs. These are the tasks the learning store exists to stabilise, and they remain the honest ceiling on a 5-rep instrument.
